properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean Carboniferous sandstone and volcanic tuff bedrock. Superstructure composed of fine-grained pale cream-to-grey Craigleith and Hailes sandstone ashlar, bedded with non-hydraulic lime mortar. Stable urban ground with historic subterranean drainage and basement lightwells.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Bordering parkland canopy featuring mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Late September phenology: full canopy structure with early chlorosis, yellowing leaf margins, and minor localized leaf drop along lower branches.

properties.architectural_summary: Georgian Neoclassical unified palatial terrace designed by Robert Adam, flanked around the central West Register House (formerly St George's Church, Robert Reid). Three-storey plus basement and attic residential bays with rusticated ground floors and ashlar upper levels. Central monument features a colossal tetrastyle Ionic portico, stepped attic base, cylindrical drum with Corinthian pilasters, and a ribbed hemispherical cupola. Fenestration consists of timber 12-pane and 6-over-6 sash-and-case windows with ashlar architraves. True plumb vertical load-bearing lines and rectified straight rooflines.
